titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§224–226: The Guard and the Day Watch
part: §§224–226 — The Guard and the Day Watch
about: Chinggis Qahan builds the imperial Guard, in 1206 as the chronicle tells it. §224 sets out how officers' sons and commoners' sons are to be brought into the Guard, with how many companions each is allowed and who pays; the penalty for evading service is exile out of sight. §225 settles the night guard and the quiver-bearers, with Jesün-Te'e, Bügidei, Qorqudaq and Lablaqa each heading a turn. §226 names the commanders of the day watch and adds up the Guard at ten thousand. Grammar to watch: the converb chains in -žu, the optative in -tuγai/-tügei, the reflexive-possessive endings (-jan, -ban, -jen), the polite plural command -dqun, and the decree frame keġen žarliγ bolba. Shiratori's quotation marks are sparse here, and the notes say where one is supplied.

sentences.t: Ulus baiγ̇ululčaγsad žobolduγsad-i miṅγad-un nojad bolγažu miṅγa minγalažu
sentences.l: Nation jointly-setting-up-ones, together-hardship-enduring-ones (acc.), of-thousands officers making, thousand thousand-ing,
sentences.i: Having made those who together founded the nation and together endured hardship officers of the thousands, and having formed the thousands,
sentences.n: The first of a long converb chain (-žu, -žü, 'having …') that runs to the decree at the end of this paragraph; I have broken it into readable units. baiγ̇ululčaγsad is baiγ̇ul- 'to set up' + -lča- 'together' + -γsad (past participle, plural: 'those who'); žobolduγsad-i adds the accusative (Ming 行, the glossators' sign of the object). nojad is the plural of noyan, 'officer' (Ming 官人); bolγažu is bol- + causative -γa- + -žu, 'having made'. miṅγa minγalažu (Ming 千 千做着) is 'thousand' then 'having thousanded', that is, having formed the thousands; 'form into units' is the reading.

morph.gloss: to set up, establish (bai- 'stand', causative) [共立了的每]
to suffer, endure hardship [共生受了的每 行]

sentences.t: miṅγad-un, žaγ̇ud-un, harbad-un nojad tüšižü tümeležü
sentences.l: Of-thousands, of-hundreds, of-tens officers appointing, ten-thousand-ing,
sentences.i: having appointed officers over the thousands, the hundreds and the tens, and having formed the ten-thousands,
sentences.n: Three genitives in a row (miṅγad-un, žaγ̇ud-un, harbad-un: -d plural + -un 'of') all qualify nojad 'officers'. tüšižü is tüši- 'to appoint, entrust' (Ming 委付) + converb -žü; tümeležü is built like minγalažu above, from tümen 'ten thousand'. Note the vowel harmony: -un after the back vowels of miṅγad, -ün after tümed (front).

sentences.t: tümed-ün nojad tüšižü
sentences.l: Of-ten-thousands officers appointing,
sentences.i: having appointed officers over the ten-thousands,
sentences.n: tümed-ün is tümen 'ten thousand' with plural -d and the front-vowel genitive -ün. The scribe repeats tüšižü after each rank; the repetition is in the text.

sentences.t: tümed-ün miṅγad-un nojad-ta sojurγal ögtekün
sentences.l: Of-ten-thousands, of-thousands to-officers favour to-be-given,
sentences.i: to the officers of the ten-thousands and the thousands, those to receive favour,
sentences.n: nojad-ta is the plural with the dative-locative -ta (Ming 行). sojurγal is the noun 'favour, grace'. ögtekün (Ming 可與的每, 'those who may be given') is ög- 'to give' with an ending -tekün that I cannot analyse with certainty; I take it as a participle of what is to be given.

morph.gloss: favour, grace (from sojurγa- 'to show favour') [恩賜]
participle of what is to be done (reading uncertain): those to be given

sentences.t: metüs-e sojurγal ögčü sojurγal žarliγ bolqun-a bolžu
sentences.l: To-kinds favour giving, favour decree to-those-doing, doing,
sentences.i: giving favour to men of such a kind, and issuing a decree of favour to those who were to do it,
sentences.n: This unit is doubtful. metüs-e has Ming 般每行, 'to those of that sort' (a metü 'kind' with plural -s and dative -e; the stem is not certain). bolqun-a is bol- + participle -qun + dative (Ming 做的每行), 'to those who do / make'. I read the whole as: giving favour to those of that sort, and making a favour-decree for those who are to carry it out. Another reading may be better.

morph.gloss: favour, grace (from sojurγa- 'to show favour') [恩賜]
favour, grace (from sojurγa- 'to show favour') [恩賜]
to do, make, be [做的每行]

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan žarliγ bolurun:
sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan decree when-making:
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan issued a decree:
sentences.n: The converb chain ends here: the subject and the finite verb 'issued a decree' are given together, žarliγ bolurun (house rendering 'issued a decree:'; bol- with -urun, 'when …ing'). The colon is Shiratori's. Qaγan is printed Qaγan in the title position; in `i` Qahan.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title of Temüjin, a man's name [太祖︀]

sentences.t: "Urida najan kebteġülsütü dalan turγaγ kešigtentü büleġe.
sentences.l: "Formerly eighty night-guards, seventy day-watch guardsman-having, were.
sentences.i: “Formerly there were eighty night guards and seventy day guards, with their guardsmen.
sentences.n: Speech begins; the opening mark is Shiratori's. -tü is the possessive suffix 'having' (Ming 有的): kebteġül-sütü, 'having night-guards', kešigten-tü, 'having guardsmen'. Ming 宿衞 for kebteġül and 散班 for turγaγ (the day watch); the exact division of the eighty and seventy is hard to see from the words alone, so I give both groups as the Ming does. büleġe is bü- 'to be' with the past -leġe, Ming 有來 'there used to be'.

morph.gloss: guardsman, member of the guard [扈衞(每)有的]

sentences.t: Edöġe müṅke teṅgeri-jin küčün-dür teṅgeri γažar-a küčü auγa nemegdežü
sentences.l: Now eternal heaven's strength-in, heaven earth-on strength might being-added,
sentences.i: Now, by the strength of Eternal Heaven, with strength and might added on the earth from Heaven,
sentences.n: teṅgeri-jin is the genitive after a vowel (-jin; the Ming glossators read it 天的, 'of Heaven'); küčün-dür is the dative-locative of küčü (Ming 氣力裏, 'in, by strength'). γažar-a has Ming 地行, the dative-locative 'to / on the earth'. nemegdežü is neme- 'to add' + passive -gde- + converb, 'being added' (Ming 被添着). Whether 'Heaven' in line 44 is the sender of strength or part of a pair 'Heaven and earth' I have read from the Ming 天 / 地行, but the syntax is uncertain.

morph.gloss: strength (stem küčün- before a case ending) [氣力 裏]

sentences.t: gür ulus-i šidurγudγažu γaγča žiluγ̇a-dur(i)-jan oroγ̇uluγsan-dur
sentences.l: All people (acc.) setting-straight, alone rein-in-own bringing-in-when,
sentences.i: and when, having set all the people in order, I alone brought them under my own management,
sentences.n: šidurγudγažu (Ming 敎直了着, 'having set straight') has a stem I cannot fully analyse; the chain -dγa- -žu looks causative. žiluγ̇a-dur(i)-jan: žiluγ̇a is 'rein' (Ming 調度, 'management, control'), dative-locative -dur, then reflexive-possessive -jan, 'under my own rein'. The i of dur(i) is printed in brackets by Shiratori. oroγ̇uluγsan-dur is oro- 'enter' + causative -γ̇ul- + participle -γsan + -dur, 'at the time of bringing in' (Ming 敎入了時).

morph.gloss: to set straight, put in order (stem uncertain) [敎直了着]
rein, management [調度裏 自的行]

sentences.t: edöġe na-dur kešigten turγaγ miṅγad miṅγad-ača ilγažu oroγ̇uludqun.
sentences.l: Now to-me guardsmen, day-watch, thousands from-thousands selecting, bring-in(polite).
sentences.i: Now, selecting guardsmen and day guards out of the thousands, bring them in to me.
sentences.n: na-dur: na- is the oblique stem of bi 'I' (Ming 我行, dative 'to me'). oroγ̇uludqun is oro- + causative -γ̇ul- + the ending -dqun, which the Ming glosses 您 and which I take as a polite plural command, 'be so good as to bring in'. miṅγad-ača is 'from the thousands' (ablative -ača; Ming 千每行). ilγažu is ilγa- 'to pick out' + converb.

morph.gloss: guardsman, member of the guard [扈衞]

sentences.t: Oroγ̇ulurun kebteġül qorčin turγaγ oroγ̇ulurun tümen düġürgen oroγ̇uludqun"
sentences.l: Bringing-in-when night-guards, quiver-bearers, day-watch, bringing-in-when ten-thousand filling, bring-in."
sentences.i: When you bring them in — night guards, quiver-bearers, day guards — bring in so as to fill ten thousand.”
sentences.n: Oroγ̇ulurun is the converb of time (-urun, 'when …ing') of the causative 'bring in'. düġürgen is düġür- 'to be full' + causative -ge- + converb -n (Ming 敎滿), 'making full'. The closing quotation mark is Shiratori's. qorčin (Ming 帶弓箭的) is the bearer of the quiver, a bowman of the guard.

morph.gloss: quiver-bearer, archer of the guard [帶弓箭的]

sentences.t: keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Saying, decree made.
sentences.i: So he issued the decree.
sentences.n: keġen is keġe- 'to say' with converb -n (Ming 麽道, 'saying'); this frames every speech in the paragraph. bolba is bol- + past -ba, 'made'.

sentences.t: Basa Čiṅgis Qaγan kešigten ilγažu oroγ̇ulqu-ji žarliγ miṅγad miṅγad-ta tuṅγarun
sentences.l: Again Chinggis Qaγan guardsmen selecting bringing-in-of decree, to-thousands when-proclaiming,
sentences.i: Again, when Chinggis Qahan proclaimed to the thousands his decree on selecting guardsmen and bringing them in, he said:
sentences.n: oroγ̇ulqu-ji žarliγ: the ending -qu is a future participle (Ming 敎入的, 'what is to be brought in') and -ji is the accusative after a vowel; the Ming does not mark it, and I read it as 'the decree about bringing in'. tuṅγarun is tuṅγa- 'to proclaim' (Ming 傳布) with the converb of time. The speech that follows has no opening mark in Shiratori; the mark in `i` is supplied here, since the closing mark at line 208 shows where it ends. 'he said' is supplied for the colon.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title of Temüjin, a man's name [太祖︀]
guardsman, member of the guard [護衞(每)]

sentences.t: bidan-dur kešigten oroγ̇ulurun tümed-ün miṅγad-un, žaγ̇ud-un nojad-un köġüd duri-jin küġün-ü köġüd ororun
sentences.l: "To-us guardsmen when-bringing-in, of-ten-thousands, of-thousands, of-hundreds, of-officers sons, plain-of people-of sons when-entering,
sentences.i: “When you bring guardsmen in to us, and the sons of the officers of the ten-thousands, thousands and hundreds, and the sons of commoners, are entering,
sentences.n: The opening mark is supplied in `i` only (Shiratori has none). bidan-dur: bida is the inclusive 'we' (oblique stem bidan-), dative-locative 'to us' (Ming 俺行). duri-jin küġün-ü, 'of a plain person' (Ming 白身人的), means a commoner, a man without rank; köġüd is köġün 'son' with plural -d. ororun is oro- + converb of time. The chain of genitives runs long; the sense is that the sons of all ranks are brought in.

morph.gloss: guardsman, member of the guard [護衞(每)]

sentences.t: erdemten šil said-i bidan-u dergede jabuqun metüs-i oroγ̇ultuγai.
sentences.l: Skilled-ones, appearance good-ones (acc.), our in-front go-ing-ones, kinds (acc.), let-them-bring-in.
sentences.i: let them bring in those of such a kind as are skilled, good in looks, and go about in our presence.
sentences.n: erdemten (Ming 技能有的每) is erdem 'skill' with the possessive -ten, 'skilled ones'; šil said-i (Ming 狀貌好的每行) is 'good in appearance' with the accusative -i. dergede (Ming 根前) is 'in front of, in the presence of', so jabuqun is 'those who go about before us', an attendant's duty. metüs-i is the same word as at line 22 (Ming 般每行 again), here with the accusative: 'such kinds'. oroγ̇ultuγai is the optative (-tuγai, Ming 者) of the causative 'bring in': 'let them be brought in'.

morph.gloss: in front of, in the presence of [根前]

sentences.t: Miṅγad-un nojad-un köġüd-i oroγ̇ulurun harban nöködtü nigen deġü in-ü daγaγ̇ulžu iletügei.
sentences.l: Of-thousands officers' sons (acc.) when-bringing-in, ten companion-having, one younger-brother his having-follow, let-bring.
sentences.i: When the sons of the officers of the thousands are brought in, each with ten companions and one younger brother of his following, let them bring them.
sentences.n: nöködtü is nökör 'companion' (plural nököd) with -tü 'having' (Ming 伴當有的), 'having ten companions'. deġü is 'younger brother'; in-ü is the genitive 'his' of the pronoun's oblique stem (Ming 他的). daγaγ̇ulžu is daγa- 'follow' + causative -γ̇ul- + converb (Ming 敎隨着), 'having him follow'. iletügei (Ming 敎來者) could be ile- 'to send / bring' and differs from iretügei at line 124, where the stem is ire- 'come'; the Ming glosses both alike, so the first may be a variant, and I translate both 'let them bring'.

sentences.t: Žaγ̇ud-un nojad-un köġüd-i oroγ̇ulurun tabun nöködtü nigen deġü-ji daγaγ̇ulžu iretügei.
sentences.l: Of-hundreds officers' sons (acc.) when-bringing-in, five companion-having, one younger-brother (acc.) having-follow, let-come.
sentences.i: When the sons of the officers of the hundreds are brought in, each with five companions and one younger brother following, let them come.
sentences.n: Same pattern as the thousands, with five companions. The younger brother stands in the accusative deġü-ji (-ji after a vowel; the Ming has 行). iretügei is ire- 'to come' + optative (Ming 敎來者), here with the verb 'come' rather than 'bring'.

sentences.t: Harbad-un nojad-un köġüd-i oroγ̇ulurun
sentences.l: Of-tens officers' sons (acc.) when-bringing-in,
sentences.i: When the sons of the officers of the tens are brought in,
sentences.n: The tens: harbad-un, as above. The lines for the tens and for commoners are given in two short units because the companions are named only after both.

sentences.t: duri-jin küġün-ü köġüd-i oroγ̇ulurun
sentences.l: Plain-of people-of sons (acc.) when-bringing-in,
sentences.i: and when the sons of commoners are brought in,
sentences.n: A parallel clause; the whole of the sentence runs on to the next unit, where a number of companions is stated for both of these groups.

sentences.t: γurban nökörtü nigen kü deġü-ji daγaγ̇ulžu
sentences.l: Three companion-having, one also younger-brother (acc.) having-follow,
sentences.i: each with three companions, and one younger brother following,
sentences.n: nökörtü here has the singular nökör 'companion' + -tü (Ming 伴當有的), where the earlier lines have the plural nököd. The particle kü (Ming 也) is an emphatic 'also, indeed', placed after nigen 'one'. Its force is slight.

sentences.t: hužaγ̇ur-ača ulaγ̇a küčü žasažu iretügei.
sentences.l: Root-from, mounts, strength preparing, let-come.
sentences.i: providing their mounts and strength from their own resources, let them come.
sentences.n: hužaγ̇ur-ača is 'from the root / origin' (Ming 根源行, perhaps 'from their own stock, at their own cost'). ulaγ̇a is the riding horse, Ming 騎坐馬匹; küčü (Ming 氣力) is 'strength', which I read as the strength of the horses and men. žasažu is žasa- 'to arrange, make ready' + converb. I read 'at their own cost', but the reading of hužaγ̇ur here is uncertain.

morph.gloss: to order, arrange, make ready [整治着]

sentences.t: Bidan-dur dergede jabuγ̇ulqun-i bökelerün
sentences.l: To-us in-front causing-to-go-ones (acc.) strength-doing-when,
sentences.i: As for those whom we have caused to serve in our presence, when they are made to show their strength,
sentences.n: jabuγ̇ulqun-i is jabu- 'go' + causative -γ̇ul- + participle -qun + accusative (Ming 敎行每的行), 'those made to go about'. bökelerün is bökele- 'to exert strength' (Ming 氣力做時) + converb of time. The sense is that when the guard is called to its duty, the rule on the next lines is to apply. Uncertain.

morph.gloss: in front of, in the presence of [根前]
to exert strength, show prowess [氣力做 時]

sentences.t: miṅγad-un nojad-un köġüd-te harban nököd hužaγ̇ur miṅγan žaγ̇un-ača qubčižu ögtügei
sentences.l: Of-thousands officers' sons-to, ten companions' root, thousand hundred-from levying, let-give.
sentences.i: to the sons of the officers of the thousands, for their ten companions' needs, levying it from the thousands and the hundreds, let it be given.
sentences.n: köġüd-te is the dative-locative plural (-te, Ming 行). The 'root, origin' hužaγ̇ur appears again (Ming 根源), here a supply for the companions. miṅγan žaγ̇un-ača, Ming 千百處, is 'from the thousands and hundreds'. qubčižu (Ming 科斂着) is qubči- 'to levy' + converb. The reading of the provision is tentative.

morph.gloss: to levy, collect in shares [科斂着]

sentences.t: ečige-jen öġügsen qubi kešig böġesü
sentences.l: Father own-given share, portion if-there-is,
sentences.i: If there is a share and portion that his own father gave him,
sentences.n: ečige-jen is ečige 'father' + reflexive-possessive -jen (Ming 父 自的行). öġügsen is ög- 'to give' + past participle -gsen. qubi and kešig (Ming 分, 子) stand together as a pair, 'share, portion'; kešig also means 'turn' or 'guard-turn' elsewhere in this paragraph, but here the Ming 子 shows the sense 'portion'. böġesü is bü- 'to be' + conditional -ġesü (Ming 有呵), 'if there is'.

sentences.t: in-ü beje γad(i)-jar oluγsan žüġegsen ere aγta kedüi böġesü in-ü
sentences.l: His self alone-obtained, set-down men, geldings however-many if-there-are,
sentences.i: and whatever number of men and animals he himself got by himself and set aside,
sentences.n: beje is 'body, self'; γad(i)-jar is the instrumental of a stem γadi (Ming 獨自 自的行), 'alone, by himself'; oluγsan and žüġegsen are past participles of olu- 'to obtain' and žüġe- 'to set, place' (Ming 得了的, 置了的). ere aγta is 'men, geldings' (Ming 人口, 頭疋), meaning people and livestock. kedüi (Ming 幾多) 'however many' + böġesü, 'if there be'. The line is read from the Ming; the exact sense of γadi is uncertain.

morph.gloss: alone, by oneself (stem uncertain) [獨自 自的行]
to set, put in place [置了的]

sentences.t: emčü qubi-ača aṅgida bidan-u kemlegsen kem(i)-jer qubčižu tein qubčižu žasažu ögtügei.
sentences.l: His own-private share-from, apart, our fixed limit-by levying, so levying, preparing, let-give.
sentences.i: apart from his own private share, levying it according to the limit that we have fixed, levying and preparing it thus, let it be given.
sentences.n: emčü qubi is 'own share' (Ming 梯已分子, 'private share'); qubi-ača is the ablative 'from the share', and aṅgida 'outside, apart from' (Ming 外). kemlegsen is the past participle of a verb 'to fix a limit' (Ming 限定了的); kem(i)-jer is 'by the limit' (Ming 限依着), the instrumental -jer. tein is 'thus'. This is the main clause of the long sentence: after the household's own share is set aside, the rest is to be levied by the fixed rule.

morph.gloss: to fix a limit, set a measure [限定了的]
to levy, collect in shares [科斂着]
to levy, collect in shares [科斂着]
to order, arrange, make ready [整治着]

sentences.t: Žaγ̇ud-un nojad-un köġüd-te tabun nököd
sentences.l: Of-hundreds officers' sons-to five companions,
sentences.i: To the sons of the officers of the hundreds, five companions;
sentences.n: The same rule for the hundreds. The provision follows below, in the mün … qubčižu ögtügei clause, 'in the same way'.

sentences.t: harbad-un nojad-un köġüd-te duri-jin küġün-ü köġüd-te γurban nököd
sentences.l: Of-tens officers' sons-to, plain-of people-of sons-to three companions,
sentences.i: to the sons of the officers of the tens and the sons of commoners, three companions;
sentences.n: A pair of datives, -te twice, for the tens and for commoners. The companions are three, as at line 133.

sentences.t: mün kü josu-γ̇ar in-ü emčü qubi- ača aṅgida mün tein qubčižu ögtügei"
sentences.l: Just also by-rule his private share-from, apart, just so levying, let-give."
sentences.i: in the same way, by the rule, apart from his private share, levy it just so, and let it be given.”
sentences.n: mün kü (Ming 只 也) is 'just, in the same way', josu-γ̇ar is josu 'rule, custom' + instrumental -γ̇ar (Ming 理依着, 'according to the rule'). The word qubi- at line 202 is cut by Shiratori at the line end and ača at 203 completes it (Ming 行), so these are one word in two. The closing mark is Shiratori's.

morph.gloss: rule, custom, what is proper [理 依着]
ablative: from (written as a separate word after qubi-) [行]
to levy, collect in shares [科斂着]

sentences.t: keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Saying, decree made.
sentences.i: So he issued the decree.
sentences.n: The frame as above.

sentences.t: "Miṅγad-un, žaγ̇ud-un, harbad-un nojad olon küġün bidan-u ene žarliγ kürġeġülüġed sonosuγ̇ad
sentences.l: "Of-thousands, of-hundreds, of-tens officers, many people, our this decree having-delivered, having-heard,
sentences.i: “The officers of the thousands, hundreds and tens, and many people, when they have delivered this decree of ours and heard it,
sentences.n: The opening mark is Shiratori's. kürġeġülüġed is kür- 'to reach' + causative -ġeġül- + converb -üġed (Ming 敎到了), 'having made it reach'; sonosuγ̇ad is sonos- 'to hear' + converb -uγ̇ad (Ming 聽了). The two converbs lead to the finite verb in the next unit.

sentences.t: bürün dabaqun haran aldaltan boltuγai.
sentences.l: If-being, transgressing-ones people penalty-having let-be.
sentences.i: then let those who transgress it be liable to penalty.
sentences.n: bürün (Ming 有呵, 'if') is bü- 'to be' with the converb of time -rün, here 'being, if'. dabaqun is daba- 'to cross, transgress' + participle -qun (Ming 越了每的). aldaltan is aldal 'fault, penalty' + -tan 'having' (Ming 罰有的每), 'having a penalty'. boltuγai is the optative 'let be'. Note this unit is the conclusion of the decree on bringing in the guard.

morph.gloss: converb of time: being, when, if

sentences.t: Bidan-dur kešig oroγ̇uldaqun haran
sentences.l: "To-us guard bringing-in-ones people,
sentences.i: “As for the people who are brought into our guard,
sentences.n: The opening mark is Shiratori's; it follows the closing mark at line 224. oroγ̇uldaqun is oro- 'enter' + causative + -daqun, which the Ming reads 敎入每; the form is hard to separate, and I take it as a participle, 'those to be brought in'. kešig here has Ming 宿衞, 'the guard'.

sentences.t: bultarižu ülü bolqun haran bidan-u dergede jabuqui-ban berkešijeġsü besu-ji oroγ̇ulžu
sentences.l: Shirking, not consenting people, our in-front go-ing (own) if-making-difficulty, others (acc.) bringing-in,
sentences.i: who shirk and are unwilling, if they find it hard to serve in our presence, and bring in others in their place,
sentences.n: bultarižu is bultari- 'to shirk, dodge' (Ming 𧻞避着) + converb. ülü bolqun (Ming 不肯的每) is 'not-consenting', ülü being the negative particle placed before the participle. jabuqui-ban is jabu- 'go' + participle + reflexive-possessive -ban, 'their own going'. berkešijeġsü is read as berkešije- 'to find hard' (Ming 作難) + conditional; the ending is unusual. besu-ji (Ming 別的行) is 'others'. The unit is hard; I give the Ming's sense.

morph.gloss: in front of, in the presence of [根前]
to go, move about [行的 自的行]
to find hard, make difficulty [作難︀呵]

sentences.t: tere küġün-i ereġülüžü nidün-ü ečine qolo γažar-a ileje"
sentences.l: That person (acc.) blaming, eye-of behind, far land-to, let-us-send."
sentences.i: that man shall be blamed, and we shall send him behind our eyes, to a far land.”
sentences.n: ereġülüžü (Ming 罪着, 'blaming') has a stem I cannot analyse; ereġül- is a guess. nidün-ü ečine (Ming 眼的背行) is 'behind the eye(s)', 'out of sight'; qolo γažar-a is 'to a far land'. ileje is ile- 'to send' + -je, a first-person hortative, 'let us send' (Ming 敎去). The closing mark is Shiratori's.

morph.gloss: to blame, hold at fault (stem uncertain) [罪着]

sentences.t: keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Saying, decree made.
sentences.i: So he issued the decree.
sentences.n: The frame again.

sentences.t: "Dotona bidan-u dergede jabužu surulčasu keġežü
sentences.l: "Inside our in-front going, together-let-us-learn, saying,
sentences.i: “‘Let us serve together in our presence within,’ saying thus,
sentences.n: The opening mark is Shiratori's. dotona (Ming 裏行) is 'inside, within'. surulčasu is sur- 'to learn' + -lča- 'together' + -su, which I take as the first-person optative (Ming 共學我, 'let us all learn'). keġežü is keġe- 'to say' + converb. The inner quotation marks in `i` are supplied, since Shiratori marks only the outer speech.

morph.gloss: in front of, in the presence of [根前]

sentences.t: bidan-dur irekün haran-i bu idγatuγai"
sentences.l: To-us coming-ones people (acc.) do-not let-them-hinder."
sentences.i: let none hinder the people who come to us.”
sentences.n: irekün is ire- 'to come' + participle -kün (Ming 來的每); bu with the optative idγatuγai is the prohibition (bu … -tuγai, Ming 休 … 者), 'let (them) not hinder'. idγa- 'to hinder, stop' (Ming 阻當). The closing mark is Shiratori's.

sentences.t: keġebe.
sentences.l: said.
sentences.i: So he said.
sentences.n: keġebe is keġe- 'to say' + past -be (Ming 說了): the speaker's decree is reported as spoken, here with 'said' rather than 'decree made'.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγ̇an-u žarliγ boluγsaγ̇ar miṅγad-ača ilγažu
sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan's decree according-to-what-was-made, from-thousands selecting,
sentences.i: According to the decree that Chinggis Qahan had made, selecting from among the thousands,
sentences.n: boluγsaγ̇ar is bol- + past participle -uγsan + instrumental -γ̇ar (Ming 做了的依着), 'according to what was done / made'. Qaγ̇an-u is the genitive of the title (Ming 皇帝的). miṅγad-ača, 'from the thousands'. The unit begins the sentence, which runs to the sons being brought in.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title of Temüjin, a man's name [太祖︀]
to do, make, be [做了的依着]

sentences.t: žaγ̇ud-un, harbad-un nojad-un köġüd-i mün kü žarlig(i)-jar ilγažu γarγažu irežü
sentences.l: Of-hundreds, of-tens officers' sons (acc.) just also by-decree selecting, bringing-out, having-come,
sentences.i: the sons of the officers of the hundreds and the tens too, selected by the decree, brought out and come,
sentences.n: žarlig(i)-jar is žarliγ 'decree' + instrumental -jar (Ming 聖旨依着), the i in brackets being Shiratori's. γarγažu is γar- 'to go out' + causative -γa- + converb (Ming 出着), 'bringing out'; irežü is ire- 'to come' + converb (Ming 來着). The sentence is a chain of converbs without a clear finite verb here; the verb is at the end of the paragraph.

sentences.t: urida najan kebteġül büleġei.
sentences.l: "Formerly eighty night-guards were.
sentences.i: “Formerly there were eighty night guards.
sentences.n: The opening mark is Shiratori's. Ming 在前八十宿衞有來. büleġei is the same as büleġe at line 39 (past of bü- 'to be').

sentences.t: Naiman žaγ̇ud bolγaba.
sentences.l: Eight hundreds he made.
sentences.i: He made them eight hundreds.
sentences.n: Naiman is printed with a capital here (Ming 八), but it is the number 'eight', not the Naiman people; the Ming gloss is simply 八, and with žaγ̇ud 'hundreds' (Ming 百每) it reads 'eight hundreds'. bolγaba is bol- + causative -γa- + past, 'made (them) become'. The speaker seems to be the narrator here; the closing quotation is at line 292, so this may be inside the speech (the mark is not in Shiratori).

sentences.t: Naiman žaγ̇ud deġere miṅγa düġürgetügei" keġebe.
sentences.l: Eight hundreds on-top thousand let-be-filled" he said.
sentences.i: “On top of the eight hundreds let the thousand be filled up,” he said.
sentences.n: The opening mark is supplied in `i` only; Shiratori prints only the closing one, at düġürgetügei. deġere (Ming 上) is 'on top of'. düġürgetügei is düġür- 'to be full' + causative -ge- + optative -tügei (Ming 敎滿者), 'let it be made full'. keġebe closes it. I cannot be sure where the speech starts.

morph.gloss: on top of, above, in addition [上]

sentences.t: "Kebteġül-dür oroqun-i bu idγatuγai"
sentences.l: "In-night-guard entering-ones (acc.) do-not let-them-hinder."
sentences.i: “Let none hinder those who enter the night guard.”
sentences.n: kebteġül-dür is 'into the night guard' (dative-locative, Ming 宿衞裏). oroqun-i is oro- + participle -qun + accusative (Ming 入的每行). bu … idγatuγai is the prohibition again, as at line 262.

sentences.t: keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Saying, decree made.
sentences.i: So he issued the decree.
sentences.n: The frame.

sentences.t: Kebteġül-i Jeke-Neġürin aqalažu miṅγa medežü atuγai" keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Night-guard (acc.) Jeke-Neġürin heading, thousand managing let-be, saying, decree made.
sentences.i: “Let Jeke-Ne'ürin be at the head of the night guard and manage the thousand.” So he issued the decree.
sentences.n: Jeke-Neġürin has Ming 人名; the Ming says nothing of his rank. aqalažu is aqala- 'to be the elder, to head' (a verb from aqa 'elder brother') + converb (Ming 爲長着). medežü is mede- 'to know' with the Ming 營着, 'running, managing' (a broadening of the usual sense). atuγai is a- 'to be' + optative (Ming 有者). The closing quotation mark is Shiratori's; no opening mark is printed, and `i` supplies it here. The Jeke here is Shiratori's spelling of Yeke.

morph.gloss: to be the elder, head, lead (from aqa 'elder brother') [爲長着]
to know; here to manage, take charge [營着]

sentences.t: "Urida dörben žaγ̇ud qorčin ilγaba.
sentences.l: "Formerly four hundreds quiver-bearers selected.
sentences.i: “Formerly I selected four hundred quiver-bearers.
sentences.n: The opening mark is Shiratori's. dörben is 'four', žaγ̇ud 'hundreds'. ilγaba is ilγa- 'to pick out' + past (Ming 選揀了). 'I' is supplied: the speaker is Chinggis.

morph.gloss: quiver-bearer, archer of the guard [帶弓箭的]

sentences.t: Ilγažu qorčin-i Želme-jin köġün Jesün-Teġe aqalažu
sentences.l: Selecting, quiver-bearers (acc.) Jelme's son Jesün-Teġe heading,
sentences.i: Having chosen them, with Jelme's son Jesün-Te'e at the head of the quiver-bearers,
sentences.n: Želme-jin is the genitive of Jelme, 'of Jelme' (Ming 人名的); köġün 'son' follows (Ming 子). qorčin-i is the accusative (Ming 帶弓箭的行). The unit stops before the second head of the quiver-bearers.

morph.gloss: Jelme, a man's name [人名 的]
to be the elder, head, lead (from aqa 'elder brother') [爲長着]

sentences.t: Tüge-jin köġün Bügidei-lüġe ejetüldüžü atuγai" keġebe.
sentences.l: Tüge's son with-Bügidei counselling-together, let-be." He-said.
sentences.i: and Tüge's son Bügidei taking counsel with him, let them be.” He said.
sentences.n: Tüge-jin köġün, 'son of Tüge'; the name Bügidei with the comitative -lüġe, 'with Bügidei' (Ming 一同). ejetüldüžü (Ming 商量着) is a counsel verb with -dü- 'together'; the stem eje- 'counsel' is a house reading. atuγai (Ming 在者) is 'let (them) be'. keġebe, 'he said'.

morph.gloss: Tüge, a man's name [人名 的]
Bügidei, a man's name [人名 一同]

sentences.t: "Turγaγ̇ud-luγ̇a qorčin kešig kešig-tür oroldurun
sentences.l: "With-day-guards, quiver-bearers turn turn-in when-entering,
sentences.i: “When the quiver-bearers enter with the day guards, turn by turn,
sentences.n: The opening mark is Shiratori's. turγaγ̇ud-luγ̇a is the plural turγaγ̇ud + comitative -luγ̇a, 'together with the day guards' (Ming 散班一同). kešig is 'turn' (Ming 班), kešig-tür the dative-locative; the repetition kešig kešig-tür seems to say 'turn by turn'. oroldurun is oro- 'enter' with reciprocal-collective -ldu- and the converb of time.

morph.gloss: quiver-bearer, archer of the guard [帶弓箭的]

sentences.t: Jesün-Teġe nigen kešig qorčin-i aqalažu orotuγai.
sentences.l: Jesün-Teġe one turn quiver-bearers (acc.) heading, let-enter.
sentences.i: let Jesün-Te'e, heading one turn of the quiver-bearers, enter.
sentences.n: nigen kešig, 'one turn' (Ming 一班). orotuγai is oro- 'enter' + optative (Ming 敎入者). The Ming 敎入 puts the sense as 'be made to enter'.

morph.gloss: to be the elder, head, lead (from aqa 'elder brother') [爲長着]

sentences.t: Bügidei nigen kešig qorčin-i aqalažu orotuγai.
sentences.l: Bügidei one turn quiver-bearers (acc.) heading, let-enter.
sentences.i: Let Bügidei, heading one turn of the quiver-bearers, enter.
sentences.n: Same pattern. Shiratori prints aqalažu as 'heading' (Ming 爲長者).

morph.gloss: to be the elder, head, lead (from aqa 'elder brother') [爲長者︀]

sentences.t: Qorqudaγ nigen kešig qorčin-i aqalažu orotuγai.
sentences.l: Qorqudaγ one turn quiver-bearers (acc.) heading, let-enter.
sentences.i: Let Qorqudaq, heading one turn of the quiver-bearers, enter.
sentences.n: Same pattern. The name is Qorqudaγ, Qorqudaq in `i`.

morph.gloss: to be the elder, head, lead (from aqa 'elder brother') [爲長着]

sentences.t: Lablaqa nigen kešig qorčin-i aqalažu orotuγai.
sentences.l: Lablaqa one turn quiver-bearers (acc.) heading, let-enter.
sentences.i: Let Lablaqa, heading one turn of the quiver-bearers, enter.
sentences.n: Same pattern. Four heads are named for the four turns, Jesün-Te'e, Bügidei, Qorqudaq and Lablaqa.

morph.gloss: to be the elder, head, lead (from aqa 'elder brother') [爲長者︀]

sentences.t: Qor aγsaquj-a turγaγ̇ud-un kešig kešig qorčin(i)-jan tein aqalažu oroγ̇ultuγai.
sentences.l: Quiver to-the-wearing, day-guards' turn turn quiver-bearers (own) so heading, let-bring-in.
sentences.i: For those who wear the quiver, let the turns of the day guards be brought in in the same way, each headed by its own quiver-bearers.
sentences.n: Doubtful. qor is 'quiver' (Ming 箭筒); aγsaquj-a is aγsa- 'to wear at the belt' + participle + dative (Ming 帶的行), 'to the wearers'. turγaγ̇ud-un kešig kešig is 'the turns of the day guards, turn by turn'; qorčin(i)-jan has the reflexive-possessive -jan (Ming 帶弓箭的自的行), 'their own quiver-bearers'. tein … aqalažu, 'so heading'. oroγ̇ultuγai is the causative optative. I read it as a general rule following the four names.

morph.gloss: to wear at the belt, carry [帶的行]
to be the elder, head, lead (from aqa 'elder brother') [爲長着]

sentences.t: Qorčin-i miṅγan düġürġežü Jesün-Teġe aqalažu atuγai"
sentences.l: Quiver-bearers (acc.) thousand filling, Jesün-Teġe heading, let-be."
sentences.i: Having made up the quiver-bearers to a thousand, let Jesün-Te'e be at their head.”
sentences.n: miṅγan is the form of 'thousand' that Shiratori prints before verbs and after quiver-bearers. düġürġežü is düġür- + causative + converb (Ming 敎滿着). The closing mark is Shiratori's, and the whole speech from line 310 closes here.

morph.gloss: to be the elder, head, lead (from aqa 'elder brother') [爲長着]

sentences.t: keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Saying, decree made.
sentences.i: So he issued the decree.
sentences.n: The frame closes §225.

sentences.t: "Urida Ögere čerbi-lüġe oroγsad turγaγ̇ud deġere miṅγan düġürġežü
sentences.l: "Formerly Ögere with-chamberlain entering-ones day-guards on-top thousand filling,
sentences.i: “Formerly the day guards who entered with Ögere the chamberlain, making up a thousand over and above,
sentences.n: The opening mark is Shiratori's. čerbi (Ming 官名) is a court office; I use 'chamberlain', a translation of convenience, with no Ming gloss for the meaning. čerbi-lüġe is the comitative 'with the čerbi'. oroγsad is oro- + past participle plural (Ming 入投的每, 'those who entered'). deġere miṅγan düġürġežü, 'on top, filling a thousand'.

morph.gloss: chamberlain (a court office) [官名 一同]
on top of, above, in addition [上]

sentences.t: Boγ̇orču-jin uruγ-ača Ögere čerbi medetügei" keġebe.
sentences.l: Boγorču's kin-from Ögere chamberlain let-manage." He-said.
sentences.i: let Ögere the chamberlain, of Bo'orchu's kin, take charge of them.” He said.
sentences.n: Boγ̇orču-jin uruγ-ača: uruγ is 'lineage, kin' (Ming 宗族), -ača the ablative, 'from Bo'orchu's kin'. medetügei is mede- 'to manage' + optative (Ming 敎管者). The grammar puts the names in apposition and the sense is that Ögere is a kinsman of Bo'orchu.

morph.gloss: Bo'orchu, a man's name [人名 的]
to know; here to manage, take charge [敎管者︀]

sentences.t: "Nigen miṅγan turγaγ̇ud-i Muqali-jin uruγ-ača
sentences.l: "One thousand day-guards (acc.) Muqali's kin-from
sentences.i: “One thousand of the day guards: from Muqali's kin
sentences.n: The opening mark is Shiratori's. The sentence is cut after uruγ-ača for the name that completes it.

sentences.t: Buqa nigen miṅγan turγaγ̇ud-i medetügei" keġebe.
sentences.l: Buqa one thousand day-guards (acc.) let-manage." He-said.
sentences.i: Buqa shall take charge of one thousand of the day guards.” He said.
sentences.n: The repeated nigen miṅγan turγaγ̇ud-i is not a slip; it is the same phrase restated in the Ming. Buqa has Ming 人名, so a man.

morph.gloss: to know; here to manage, take charge [敎管者︀]

sentences.t: Iluγai-jin uruγ-ača Alčidai-ji nigen miṅγan turγaγ̇ud-i medetügei" keġebe.
sentences.l: Iluγai's kin-from Alchidai (acc.) one thousand day-guards (acc.) let-manage." He-said.
sentences.i: From the line of Iluqai, let Alchidai manage one thousand of the day guards.” He said.
sentences.n: Iluγai-jin uruγ-ača, 'from Iluqai's kin'. Alčidai-ji is a name in the accusative -ji (Ming 行); I read the accusative as marking the man who is given the charge, 'let (them) be put to Alchidai's charge'. The grammar here is loose and the opening mark was not printed.

morph.gloss: to know; here to manage, take charge [敎管者︀]

sentences.t: "Nigen miṅγan turγaγ̇ud-i Dodai čerbi medetügei.
sentences.l: "One thousand day-guards (acc.) Dodai chamberlain let-manage.
sentences.i: “One thousand of the day guards: let Dodai the chamberlain manage them.
sentences.n: The opening mark is Shiratori's.

morph.gloss: to know; here to manage, take charge [敎管者︀]

sentences.t: Nigen miṅγan turγaγ̇ud-i Doqolqu čerbi medetügei" keġebe.
sentences.l: One thousand day-guards (acc.) Doqolqu chamberlain let-manage." He-said.
sentences.i: One thousand of the day guards: let Doqolqu the chamberlain manage them.” He said.
sentences.n: The same, with Doqolqu. The closing mark is Shiratori's.

morph.gloss: to know; here to manage, take charge [敎管者︀]

sentences.t: "Nigen miṅγan turγaγ̇ud-i Žürčedei-jin uruγ-ača Čanai medetügei.
sentences.l: "One thousand day-guards (acc.) Jürchedei's kin-from Chanai let-manage.
sentences.i: “One thousand of the day guards: from Jürchedei's kin, let Chanai manage them.
sentences.n: Žürčedei-jin uruγ-ača, 'from Jürchedei's kin'. The opening mark is Shiratori's.

morph.gloss: to know; here to manage, take charge [管者︀]

sentences.t: Nigen miṅγan turγaγ̇ud-i Alči-jin uruγ-ača Aqutai medetügei.
sentences.l: One thousand day-guards (acc.) Alchi's kin-from Aqutai let-manage.
sentences.i: One thousand of the day guards: from Alchi's kin, let Aqutai manage them.
sentences.n: Alči-jin uruγ-ača, 'from Alchi's kin'.

morph.gloss: to know; here to manage, take charge [敎管者︀]

sentences.t: Nigen miṅγan turγaγ̇ud-i Arγai-Qasar
sentences.l: One thousand day-guards (acc.) Arγai-Qasar,
sentences.i: One thousand of the day guards: Arqai-Qasar,
sentences.n: Arγai-Qasar has Ming 人名 and no title. The unit is cut so the next one has the verb.

sentences.t: nigen miṅγan ilγaγsan baγ̇atud-i medežü olon üdür turγaγ boltuγai.
sentences.l: One thousand selected brave-men (acc.) managing, many days day-watch let-be.
sentences.i: taking charge of a thousand picked heroes, let them be the day watch for many days.
sentences.n: ilγaγsan is ilγa- 'to pick out' + past participle (Ming 選揀來的); baγ̇atud-i is the plural of baγ̇atur 'hero' (Ming 勇士每行) + accusative, 'heroes'. olon üdür is 'many days' (Ming 多日). turγaγ boltuγai, 'let (them) be the day guard'.

morph.gloss: to pick out, select [選揀來的]
hero, brave man (plural baγ̇atud) [勇士每 行]
to know; here to manage, take charge [管着]

sentences.t: qadqulduγ̇an üdür urida baižu baγ̇atud boltuγai"
sentences.l: Fighting-of day front standing, heroes let-be."
sentences.i: On the day of fighting, standing in front, let them be heroes.”
sentences.n: qadqulduγ̇an is qadqul- 'to fight one another' (Ming 厮殺) + an ending -duγ̇an that I read as a participle, 'of the fighting'; the form is doubtful. baižu is bai- 'to stand' + converb (Ming 立着). urida, 'in front'. The closing mark is Shiratori's.

morph.gloss: to fight one another, clash [厮殺︀的]

sentences.t: keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Saying, decree made.
sentences.i: So he issued the decree.
sentences.n: The frame.

sentences.t: Miṅγad miṅγad-ača ilγažu iregsed naiman miṅγad turγaγ̇ud bolba.
sentences.l: Thousands from-thousands selecting having-come eight thousands day-guards made.
sentences.i: He made eight thousands of day guards of those who had come, selected from the thousands.
sentences.n: iregsed is ire- 'to come' + past participle plural (Ming 來了的每). naiman miṅγad is 'eight thousands' (Ming 八千每), so 'eight thousand' day guards.

sentences.t: Kebteġül qorčin-luγ̇a qojar kü miṅγad bolba.
sentences.l: Night-guard with-quiver-bearers two also thousands made.
sentences.i: The night guard together with the quiver-bearers he made two thousands.
sentences.n: qorčin-luγ̇a is the comitative (Ming 帶弓箭 一同). qojar kü miṅγad, 'two thousands' (Ming 兩箇也千每), with kü 'also' emphatic. The total, eight, two, then the ten-thousand guard of the next lines.

sentences.t: Tümen kešigten bolba.
sentences.l: Ten-thousand guardsmen made.
sentences.i: He made ten thousand guardsmen.
sentences.n: Tümen kešigten (Ming 萬護衞每), 'ten thousand guardsmen', the whole Guard, being the eight and two thousands added.

morph.gloss: guardsman, member of the guard [護衞每]

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan žarliγ bolurun:
sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan decree when-making:
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan issued a decree:
sentences.n: The same frame as line 29.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title of Temüjin, a man's name [太祖︀]

sentences.t: "Bidan-u čaγ̇ada tümen kešigten-i bökeležü
sentences.l: "Our near ten-thousand guardsmen (acc.) strength-doing,
sentences.i: “Our ten thousand guardsmen, close beside us, showing their strength,
sentences.n: The opening mark is Shiratori's. čaγ̇ada (Ming 貼身) is 'close, at the side of the person', dative-locative of a noun čaγ̇a. kešigten-i has the accusative -i. bökeležü, 'showing strength'.

morph.gloss: nearness, side of the person [貼身]
to exert strength, show prowess [氣力做着]

sentences.t: jeke γol bolun atuγai"
sentences.l: Great centre being, let-remain."
sentences.i: let them be the great centre and remain so.”
sentences.n: jeke γol (Ming 大中軍) is 'the great centre, main body'; bolun is bol- + converb -un (Ming 敎做), 'becoming'. atuγai 'let (them) stay'. The closing mark is Shiratori's.

sentences.t: keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Saying, decree made.
sentences.i: So he issued the decree.
sentences.n: The frame closes §226.
